resolutions.researcher_notes: Enbridge's own asset fact sheet (PDF, verified via pdftotext) states: 'Placed into service in November 2018, the Valley Crossing Pipeline provides additional, much-needed market access for domestic supplies of clean-burning natural gas.' Oil & Gas Journal (Jan 19, 2022) describes the '160-mile' pipeline as an existing, currently-operating asset being expanded ('Enbridge to expand Valley Crossing pipeline'), confirming ongoing operating status as of 2022. Two distinct publishers (Enbridge, OGJ) agree the line is operating.

Enbridge fact sheet: transports 'clean-burning natural gas.' Brownsville Herald (Dec 16, 2017, live page now redirects; content confirmed via Wayback snapshot 20171222052250, fetched by curl and stripped of markup): pipeline built 'to supply fracked natural gas to Mexico from the Eagle Ford Shale.' Two distinct publishers agree on the fuel.

CONCERN: found sourcing for the construction timeline, but it conflicts with the sheet's ConstructionYear=2018. Brownsville Herald (Dec 16, 2017, via Wayback) reports CFE awarded VCP the construction contract in June 2016 and 'construction began last April' (i.e., April 2017); as of that Dec-2017 article, Enbridge spokesman Devin Hotzel said construction would 'continue into the second quarter of 2018' before the Rio Grande Valley segment was complete. So construction spanned 2017-2018 (in-service per other sources Nov 2018), and no source pins a single '2018' construction-start year cleanly — the earliest documented construction activity is 2017. Not proposing a ref against the sheet's stated value; leaving for Update to reconcile whether ConstructionYear should reflect 2017 (start) vs a 2018 completion-of-construction reading.

CONCERN: sheet has StartYear1=2019, but two independent sources place the in-service date in November 2018, not 2019. (1) Enbridge's own asset fact sheet (verified via pdftotext): 'Placed into service in November 2018...'. (2) Seeking Alpha's own article title/headline (Nov 2, 2018, seed citation) reads 'Enbridge places Valley Crossing Texas-to-Mexico gas pipeline into service' -- dated Nov 2, 2018 (could not fetch full article text, blocked 403 with no Wayback capture available, but the dated headline itself is strong independent corroboration of a Nov-2018 in-service date). The Brownsville Herald (Dec 2017) separately reported an *expected* in-service date of 'October 2018.' All evidence converges on late 2018, not 2019. Declining to cite a ref against the sheet's 2019 value; flagging for Update to check whether 2019 reflects a different milestone (e.g., full contractual ramp-up) or is a data error.

Enbridge fact sheet: 'transporting up to 2.6 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d)' = 2,600 MMcf/d, matching the sheet exactly. Brownsville Herald (Dec 2017, via Wayback): 'capacity of up to 2.6 billion cubic feet of natural gas per day.' Two distinct publishers agree.

CONCERN: three independent sources give three different lengths, none matching the sheet's 171.00 mi: Brownsville Herald (Dec 2017, via Wayback) says '168-mile-long'; Oil & Gas Journal (Jan 2022) says '160-mile'; SaveRGV (savergv.org, accessed 2023 per wiki) says '165 miles long.' All are close but below the sheet's figure -- plausibly a measurement-convention difference (mainline only vs. mainline+laterals/offshore Border Crossing segment, per SaveRGV's note that 'the final 1,000 feet' is filed separately with FERC as a distinct Border Crossing Project). Declining to cite any of these three as support for the sheet's exact 171.00 mi value; flagging the range (160-168 mi across sources) for Update.

Oil & Gas Journal (Jan 2022): pipeline consists of '42- and 48-in. OD' sections. SaveRGV (savergv.org): '165 miles long and varies at either 42" or 48"' in diameter. Both independently confirm the dual 42/48-inch diameter exactly as recorded on the sheet.

Brownsville Herald (Dec 2017, via Wayback): 'The pipeline will receive gas from the Agua Dulce gas hub in Nueces County' (matches StartLocation=Agua Dulce, Texas) and its 'southern terminus [is] several miles offshore at the U.S.-Mexico border,' connecting to the Sur de Texas-Tuxpan pipeline -- consistent with EndLocation=Gulf of Mexico, Texas (the offshore US-side maritime border crossing point). OGJ (Jan 2022) independently confirms the pipeline runs 'from Agua Dulce hub in Texas to the Port of Brownsville' before crossing to Mexico, corroborating the Agua Dulce start point and the Brownsville-area/Gulf-of-Mexico end point.

Brownsville Herald (Dec 2017, via Wayback) opens with 'The $1.5 billion pipeline, being built by VCP parent company Enbridge Inc.' -- rounds from the sheet's precise $1,550,000,000. Single source only (could not find a second outlet stating the project cost, so leaving independent=false and tier at medium rather than high).

Brownsville Herald (Dec 2017, via Wayback): 'VCP is wholly owned by Valley Crossing Pipeline LLC,' whose parent is Enbridge Inc. (the article's lede: 'VCP parent company Enbridge Inc.'). OGJ (Jan 2022) independently states 'Enbridge Inc. operates the pipeline.' Enbridge's own fact sheet lists Valley Crossing among its owned/operated assets. Two distinct publishers agree on 100% Enbridge ownership.
